title: Helm, Kustomize, CRDs and Operators

header.html: Use Helm and Kustomize to install cluster components; Understand CRDs, install and configure operators
Kubernetes v1.37.0, Helm 4.3.1 (checksum verified), kubectl built-in Kustomize v5.8.1. Run helm version on the exam host: the basic commands below are the ones the docs at helm.sh/docs describe.

html:
1Helm in one page

Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes. A chart is a package of templated manifests. A release is one installation of a chart in a cluster. Values (values.yaml plus your overrides) fill the templates. Every install, upgrade and rollback creates a new revision.

Task Command
Add a repository helm repo add <name> <url> then helm repo update
Search a repository helm search repo <word> (add --versions for all chart versions)
See default values helm show values <chart>
Install helm install <release> <chart> -n <ns> --create-namespace --set key=val
Install from a values file helm install <release> <chart> -f myvalues.yaml
List releases helm list -n <ns> (-A for all namespaces)
Upgrade helm upgrade <release> <chart> -n <ns> --set key=val
History helm history <release> -n <ns>
Roll back helm rollback <release> <revision> -n <ns>
Remove helm uninstall <release> -n <ns>
Render without installing helm template <release> <chart> --set key=val
Values you supplied helm get values <release> (--all adds chart defaults)
The manifests in the cluster helm get manifest <release>

Facts that are tested:

  • --set overrides one value (--set replicaCount=3); nested keys use dots (service.port=8080). Never edit the chart to change a value.
  • A rollback is a new revision. After upgrade (revision 2) and rollback 1, helm history shows revision 3 with the description "Rollback to 1" (Lab 4.2).
  • Release names are namespaced. Always pass -n for a release that is not in the current namespace; helm list shows only the current namespace.
  • helm template and helm install --dry-run show output and create nothing.
  • Naming: in a chart made by helm create webapp, the Deployment is named <release>-webapp.

2Kustomize in one page

Kustomize customizes plain YAML without templates. It is built into kubectl: kubectl kustomize <dir> prints the result, kubectl apply -k <dir> applies it. A directory with a kustomization.yaml is a base; an overlay points to a base and changes it.

# overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml
resources:
- ../../base
namespace: prod            # puts every object in this namespace
namePrefix: prod-          # renames web -> prod-web (and fixes references)
replicas:
- {name: web, count: 3}
images:
- {name: nginx, newTag: stable-alpine}
Field Effect
resources the base directories or files to include
namespace, namePrefix, nameSuffix, commonLabels applied to all objects
replicas change the replica count of a named workload
images change image name or tag
patches strategic-merge or JSON patches for anything else
configMapGenerator, secretGenerator make ConfigMaps and Secrets (with a name hash)

Workflow: write the overlay, run kubectl kustomize to look at the output first, create the namespace if it does not exist (Kustomize does not create it), then kubectl apply -k. The base stays unchanged (Lab 4.5).

3Helm or Kustomize?

Helm Kustomize
Idea templates + values, versioned releases patches on plain YAML
Rollback helm rollback none (use git)
Typical exam task install a chart, upgrade, roll back, set a value build an overlay

4CRDs

A CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) teaches the API server a new resource type. After the CRD is installed, you can create custom resources (CRs) of that kind like any object.

apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: crontabs.stable.example.com     # must be <plural>.<group>
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  scope: Namespaced                      # or Cluster
  names: {plural: crontabs, singular: crontab, kind: CronTab, shortNames: [ct]}
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema: {type: object, properties: {spec: {type: object, properties: {cronSpec: {type: string}, image: {type: string}}}}}
  • The CRD metadata.name must be <plural>.<group>.
  • Wait until it is Established: kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/<name>.
  • Then: kubectl get crontabs, kubectl get ct, kubectl explain crontab.spec.
  • With a schema, the API server rejects fields it does not know (the object fails validation).
  • Find CRDs: kubectl get crd; the API group of a resource: kubectl api-resources.

5Operators

An operator is a controller plus its CRDs that automates running an application (install, backup, upgrade, failover). You install the operator (often with Helm or a manifest), then you create a custom resource that states what you want, and the operator makes it so. On the exam you install an operator the way the task says (Helm chart or manifest), create or edit its custom resource, and check the result. Troubleshooting an operator is troubleshooting its Pod: kubectl -n <ns> logs deploy/<operator>.

6Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m04 -->

Lab 4.1: helm install

Domain: Architecture | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m04-01-helm-install)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

A Helm chart exists in the directory ~/charts/webapp. Install it as the release shop in the namespace helm-ns (create the namespace if needed) with 2 replicas, by overriding the chart value replicaCount on the command line (do not edit the chart).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

helm install shop ~/charts/webapp -n helm-ns --create-namespace --set replicaCount=2 --wait --timeout 120s
helm list -n helm-ns

Lab 4.2: helm upgrade rollback

Domain: Architecture | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m04-02-helm-upgrade-rollback)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The release app (chart ~/charts/webapp) is installed in the namespace helm-ns with 1 replica. First upgrade the release so that it runs 3 replicas. Then the change turns out to be a mistake: roll the release back to its first revision. At the end the release must run 1 replica and the history must show the upgrade and the rollback.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

helm upgrade app ~/charts/webapp -n helm-ns --set replicaCount=3 --wait --timeout 120s
helm history app -n helm-ns
helm rollback app 1 -n helm-ns --wait --timeout 120s
helm history app -n helm-ns

Lab 4.3: helm values uninstall

Domain: Architecture | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m04-03-helm-values-uninstall)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Two releases exist in the namespace helm-ns: old and keep. Remove the release old completely. Save the user-supplied values of the release keep (not the chart defaults) to the file ~/answers/keep-values.yaml.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

helm list -n helm-ns
helm uninstall old -n helm-ns
helm get values keep -n helm-ns > ~/answers/keep-values.yaml
cat ~/answers/keep-values.yaml

Lab 4.4: helm template

Domain: Architecture | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m04-04-helm-template)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Without installing anything, render the manifests of the chart ~/charts/webapp for a release named preview with 4 replicas and save the output to ~/answers/rendered.yaml.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

helm template preview ~/charts/webapp --set replicaCount=4 > ~/answers/rendered.yaml
grep -E "replicas|name: preview" ~/answers/rendered.yaml

Lab 4.5: kustomize overlay

Domain: Architecture | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m04-05-kustomize-overlay)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

A Kustomize base exists in ~/kust/base (a Deployment web with 1 replica and a Service web). Create an overlay in ~/kust/overlays/prod that reuses the base and changes: namespace prod, a name prefix prod-, 3 replicas, and the container image to nginx:stable-alpine. Do not edit the base. Create the namespace prod, then apply the overlay to the cluster.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

cat > ~/kust/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml <<Y
resources:
- ../../base
namespace: prod
namePrefix: prod-
replicas:
- {name: web, count: 3}
images:
- {name: nginx, newTag: stable-alpine}
Y
kubectl kustomize ~/kust/overlays/prod | head -30
kubectl create ns prod
kubectl apply -k ~/kust/overlays/prod
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment prod-web --timeout=120s

Lab 4.6: crd custom resource

Domain: Architecture | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m04-06-crd-custom-resource)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The file ~/crd/crontab-crd.yaml defines a CustomResourceDefinition for the kind CronTab (group stable.example.com). Install it in the cluster. Then create a CronTab custom resource named nightly in the namespace default with spec.cronSpec: "0 2 * * *" and spec.image: backup:1.0. Finally write the full name of the CRD (the value in the NAME column of kubectl get crd) to ~/answers/crd-name.txt.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl apply -f ~/crd/crontab-crd.yaml
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/crontabs.stable.example.com --timeout=60s
kubectl apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: CronTab
metadata: {name: nightly}
spec:
  cronSpec: "0 2 * * *"
  image: backup:1.0
Y
kubectl get crd | grep crontabs
echo crontabs.stable.example.com > ~/answers/crd-name.txt

<!-- /LABS -->

7Recall questions

R1What is the difference between a chart and a release?

Show the answer

A chart is the package; a release is one installation of it in a cluster.

R2How do you change one chart value at install time without editing the chart?

Show the answer

--set key=value (or -f values.yaml).

R3After helm upgrade and helm rollback 1, how many revisions exist?

Show the answer

Three; the rollback is a new revision.

R4Which command shows only the values the user supplied?

Show the answer

helm get values <release> (without --all).

R5How do you preview manifests without touching the cluster?

Show the answer

helm template, or kubectl kustomize for Kustomize.

R6Does Kustomize create the target namespace?

Show the answer

No; create it first.

R7What must a CRD's metadata.name look like?

Show the answer

<plural>.<group>.

R8What is an operator?

Show the answer

A controller with CRDs that automates managing an application.
